name: The Emergence of Modern Human Behaviour: The Pleistocene Occupation Sites of South Africa
description: Three caves and rock shelters in South Africa, two in the Western Cape (Diepkloof and Pinnacle Point) and one in KwaZulu-Natal (Sibhudu), hold some of the richest traces of early human creativity. Layers of debris here go back up to 162,000 years. They contain ochre pigments, engraved ostrich eggshell, shell beads and finely made stone tools, which show that people were thinking symbolically long ago.
